summary: Reviewed 1 file (DapperBookmarkPresetRepository.cs). 0 Critical, 0 High findings. Security sign-off: PASS. Primary security surface is SQL injection risk — all four SQL strings are hardcoded constants; all user-supplied values (Label, PresetId) are passed as Dapper named parameters via anonymous objects, not concatenated. LAST_INSERT_ID() session isolation is safe due to per-call connection creation. All OWASP Top 10 categories reviewed; no blocking issues found.

comments.note: A03 — SQL Injection (MITIGATED): All four SQL constants in DapperBookmarkPresetRepository are hardcoded strings with no user-input concatenation. InsertSql uses @Label and DeleteSql uses @PresetId as named placeholders passed via Dapper anonymous-object parameters (lines 59, 77). Dapper sends these as properly parameterized queries to the database driver. No SQL injection surface exists.

A04 — Insecure Design (INFO): InsertAsync uses LAST_INSERT_ID() on the same connection as the preceding INSERT (lines 58–64). Because each method opens a fresh connection via using var connection = await _connectionFactory.CreateOpenConnectionAsync (line 54), the session is isolated to this call stack. No cross-request ID leakage risk from concurrent inserts on the same session. Pattern is safe.

summary: Reviewed 2 files: DapperBookmarkPresetRepository.cs and Program.cs (registration section). No blocking issues. All 3 ACs met. Implementation is exemplary for this codebase — strict adherence to the established Dapper repository pattern (per-call connection, CommandDefinition, ConfigureAwait, using var). SQL injection is fully mitigated via parameterized queries. InsertAsync guard style is stronger than some existing repositories. The only open item is DeleteAsync missing a presetId > 0 guard, which is a low-priority behavioral decision already flagged by QA — Developer scope for a future hardening pass.

comments.note: DapperBookmarkPresetRepository adheres precisely to the established Dapper repository pattern: per-call connection via IDbConnectionFactory, CommandDefinition with cancellationToken on every query, .ConfigureAwait(false) throughout, and using var for connection lifetime. The pattern is identical to SpdbConfigRepository — no divergence.

InsertAsync constructor guards (ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull + ArgumentException.ThrowIfNullOrEmpty) are consistent with the interface contract doc, which explicitly requires Label to be set. This is a stronger guard style than some existing repositories (e.g. SpdbConfigRepository has no null check on its constructor parameter). The pattern set here is preferable for new repositories.

DeleteAsync: no presetId > 0 guard — a negative or zero ID silently fires a no-op DELETE. This is a behavioral decision (throw vs no-op for invalid input). Since adding the guard would change behavior, this is Developer scope for a future hardening pass, not a Fix-Forward. QA and Security Auditor have both noted it as low priority and acceptable.
